title: Resource
description: A file the site hosts for people to download: a character sheet, a form to fill in, a reference to print. This describes the file. The file itself sits beside it.

name.description: What the resource is called on the shelf.

blurb.description: One line telling a reader what this is, so they can decide whether they want it. Leave it blank and the tile just shows the name.

file.description: The file's own name, which is also the address it is served from. PDFs only.

pages.description: How many pages the file has, so a reader knows what they are downloading before they download it.

fillable.description: Tick this when the file has boxes a reader can type into, rather than blanks to print and write on. Two sheets can be otherwise identical, so the site cannot work this out from the name.

sanitized.description: Tick this when the file here is a rebuilt copy rather than the original. The site tells readers so, because a file that has been altered should not be presented as the author's untouched work.

removed.description: What the rebuild took out, in words a reader will understand. Only used when the file is marked as rebuilt. Leaving it empty says the file was rebuilt and had nothing active in it.

order.description: Where this sits on the shelf. Number them 1, 2, 3 and so on with no repeats, so the order cannot change on its own.

accent.description: The hue it is drawn in, matching the palette a book may use.

credit.description: Who made it. These are somebody's work, re-hosted with permission, and the site should say whose.

sourceUrl.description: Where the file came from, so nobody has to remember later.
